Overall pass^1: native 0.979, LangChain 0.979. Mean paired difference 0.000, 90 percent CI [0.000, 0.000], equivalence margin plus or minus 0.05. H1 verdict: CONFIRMED.

Pooled pass^1 with exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95 percent intervals: native 94 of 96, [0.927, 0.997]; langchain 94 of 96, [0.927, 0.997].

What the H1 test can detect: every per-task paired difference is exactly 0, so the standard deviation is 0 and the interval collapses to [0, 0]. Both arms run the same deterministic policy against the same seeded failure draws, so any arm that loses no state reproduces the other's outcomes exactly. The test therefore rules out orchestration-caused success loss (lost state, budget overruns, corrupted resumes) on these fixtures; it carries no information about reasoning quality or about behaviour with a model in the loop.

## Axis 3: cost

| Measure | Native | LangChain |
|---|---|---|
| Policy invocations per run, median | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| Policy invocations per run, p95 | 8.0 | 8.0 |
| Wall seconds per run, median | 0.869 | 0.398 |
| Wall seconds per run, p95 | 1.488 | 0.649 |
| Durable state bytes per run, median | 16384 | 8192 |

Ratios, LangChain to native: invocations 1.000, wall 0.459 (frozen tax factor 1.10, no-tax line 1.00). H2 verdict: REFUTED.

Uncertainty on the wall ratio: paired bootstrap 95 percent interval [0.414, 0.497] (10000 resamples of the 96 task-and-seed pairs, seed 20261108). Paired sign test: LangChain was slower in 0 pairs and faster in 96 of 96 non-tied pairs, two-sided p = 2.5e-29. Both describe this one suite pass on one machine; the native arm commits synchronously after every step, and a WAL-mode or batched-commit native variant is untested, so the ordering is implementation-sensitive.

## Cross-study placement: LangChain direct beside LangGraph

Same task suite, same scripted policy, same native control design, same machine. The LangGraph column is the sibling study's published result (JesunAhmadUshno/langgraph-vs-native-study, RESULTS.md); the native column in that study is a separate run of the identical native implementation, so small wall-time differences between the two native columns are run-to-run variation on a shared machine, not a design difference.

| Measure | Native (this study) | LangChain direct (this study) | LangGraph (sibling, published) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overall pass^1 | 0.979 | 0.979 | 0.979 |
| pass^4, averaged over tasks | 0.917 | 0.917 | 0.917 |
| Median wall seconds per run | 0.869 | 0.398 | 0.293 |

| Durable state bytes per run, median | 16384 | 8192 | 36864 |
